evidence: The reviewer asked for the reshape to be called out; the agent quotes the PR body already stating "`resolved.dropped` widens from a list of switch names to records", and the field shipped one PR earlier (#12) under an epic that explicitly rules out back-compat. The shape change is real but the claimed defect (uncalled-out break of a settled contract) is not.

The `named` comparison did cross the expansion boundary; the agent reproduced that `--${CROM_PROFILE}-x=1` plus `--dev-x=2` emitted both switches, a pre-existing duplicate-emission bug, and f7e9068 refuses `${` in a flags switch half via the same `_interpolates` predicate drops already used, which removes the case rather than patching the comparison.
guidance_note: When a rule (no `${` in a switch name) is enforced on one list a parser reads, check whether every other list keyed by the same switch name needs the same border rule before writing code that compares across it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: f7e9068 touched only flags.py and test_resolve.py; the hard-coded `"[defaults] must be a table"` f-string at config.py:547 was left by the original PR's DEFAULTS_STANZA sweep, which the agent admits matched only standalone literals. Fixed in 5f86f95 along with the `[defaults].seed` label in cli.py.
guidance_note: When introducing a constant to replace a literal, grep for the literal's text inside f-strings and compound labels, not only as a standalone string token.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: f7e9068 did not touch Resolution or the dropped line; the agent reproduced `(dropped --window-size, from [defaults] ...)` with 800,600 nowhere, a gap from the original PR. The fix (5f86f95) put `value` on the shared Resolution.describe() rather than special-casing Removed, but added a docstring claiming `value` is "redundant for an emitted plain flag", which F6-F8 then found false.
guidance_note: When a rendering omits a field because a sibling channel carries it, check every consumer of the type for that sibling channel before shipping; Removed had none.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the untested `·`-join across layers is original-PR cli._note code, untouched by f7e9068; the agent confirms `_override_project` only exercises one-layer joins and adds a CLI test where one --disable-features carries ChromeWhatsNewUI from policy and PictureInPicture from [defaults].
guidance_note: When a ticket exists for one specific shape (one switch carrying names from several layers), write the CLI-level test for exactly that shape in the original PR.

evidence: 5f86f95 (F4's fix) added both `"value": self.stands.value` and the docstring "`value` is redundant for an emitted plain flag", while resolve.py's existing comment says answers stay unexpanded on purpose, so the claim was false for any `${...}` value on arrival. The agent rejected expanding answers (it would make the `over` clause unsearchable and the dropped line untrue) and instead renamed to `said`, rendered stands/over through one Answer.describe(), and pinned the divergence with a test.
guidance_note: Before writing a docstring asserting two fields are redundant, read the producer of each; resolve.py's "answers stay unexpanded" comment contradicted the claim.

evidence: Duplicate of F6 on the same line: the false redundancy docstring and the `value` field both came from 5f86f95, F4's fix. The reviewer offered "correct the docstring ... and add a test"; the agent did that plus the `said` rename and uniform answer shape in 36a076f.
guidance_note: Before writing a docstring asserting two fields are redundant, read the producer of each; resolve.py's "answers stay unexpanded" comment contradicted the claim.

evidence: Third copy of F6, anchored at cli.py's JSON payload: `flags[].flag` expanded versus `why[].value` unexpanded contradicts the redundancy docstring 5f86f95 added. Resolved by the same 36a076f rename and docstring rewrite.
guidance_note: Before writing a docstring asserting two fields are redundant, read the producer of each; resolve.py's "answers stay unexpanded" comment contradicted the claim.

evidence: f7e9068 (F2's fix) made flags.layer refuse `${` in a switch name, but README's interpolation paragraph still said "Flags and env values can interpolate" and the flags row said nothing; 36a076f narrowed it to "Flag values and env values" and documented the refusal in the flags row.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new refusal at a parse border, update the user-facing reference that describes that input (README flags row and interpolation paragraph) in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 5f86f95 did not touch resolve.py; the comment claiming "a [defaults] that sets features and no flags has an empty layer" is original-PR text. The agent confirmed parse_layer always passes origin=where, so the scenario is unreachable, and rewrote the justification in 36a076f.
guidance_note: When a comment justifies a design choice with a concrete scenario, trace the code path (here parse_layer's unconditional call) to confirm the scenario can occur before writing it.

evidence: The agent shows pyproject pins click>=8.3.1, CliRunner's params lack mix_stderr (removed in 8.2), and a probe gives separate stdout='OUT\n' stderr='ERR\n', so `.stderr` does not raise. The flag is a false positive: the test is original-PR code untouched by 5f86f95. The same test was nonetheless vacuous for a different reason (wrong cwd), which F12 found a round later.
guidance_note: When defending a test against a finding, re-run it with a mutation that should make it fail; that would have exposed the cwd bypass F12 later found on this same test.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 36a076f did not change test_config_of_a_config_that_overrides_nothing...; the direct `self.runner.invoke` bypassing the chdir helper is original-PR code. The agent instrumented it ("Here, crom is in the 'user' namespace"), made `invoke(cwd=...)` the only path as the reviewer's helper-variant option suggested, and mutation-tested the corrected test.
guidance_note: When a test helper returns the wrong projection (output, not stderr), extend the helper rather than reaching past it, and assert the scope/namespace the test believes it is in.

narrative: A provenance feature for `crom config` went through five rounds. Two fixes produced follow-on findings: F4's fix added a docstring calling `value` redundant with the emitted flag, false for any interpolated value, which drew three duplicate findings (F6-F8). F2's fix added a switch-name refusal without updating the README (F9). Every round also carried findings against original-PR code (F10, F11, F12), so no round was avoidable. F12 showed that a test the agent had correctly defended in F11 was vacuous for another reason.
guidance_observations: The agent's pushbacks (F1 contract scope, F11 click version) were both checked against artifacts and held up.
The agent correctly widened F2 into a pre-existing duplicate-emission bug, but did not sweep the user docs for the new rule in the same commit.
Defending a test on one ground (F11) without mutation-testing it let a vacuous test survive two more rounds.

evidence: The "Where a key may appear" table was duplicated verbatim in main() and config_cmd() docstrings, and the new test only checks each key is named somewhere, so drift would stay green; 254e0b0 replaces main()'s copy with a pointer to `crom config --help`.
guidance_note: When adding reference text to two help surfaces, keep it in one and point to it from the other from the start.

evidence: The reply-hint says pushback but the reply opens "agreed, and confirmed — `[defaults] port = 9401` is rejected with unknown key(s)"; the agent scoped the layering rule per key and also found drop_flags accumulates rather than profile-over-defaults, which the reviewer had missed.
guidance_note: When writing a universal claim ("every key resolves the same way") in a reference, check it per key against the parser's key sets before publishing it.

evidence: The agent confirmed `drop_flags = ["--disable-features"]` is refused ("no layer supplies it for a drop to remove") while the doc said only `flags`; 254e0b0 names both lists, matching the identity-switch paragraph above it.
guidance_note: When documenting a refusal, derive the list of inputs it applies to from the enforcing table (RESERVED_SWITCHES) rather than from memory.

evidence: `_NAME_RE` is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}\Z`, which forbids a leading `.`/`_`/`-`; the doc omitted it. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply opens "agreed" and 254e0b0 adds the leading-character and 64-char constraints.
guidance_note: When a reference states an input grammar, transcribe it from the validating regex, including anchors and length bounds.

evidence: Same line and same `_NAME_RE` gap as F4, adding the 64-character cap; fixed together in 254e0b0.
guidance_note: When a reference states an input grammar, transcribe it from the validating regex, including anchors and length bounds.

narrative: A docs-only PR expanding `--help` into a config reference drew five findings in one round. All were real accuracy gaps against the parser and validators. The agent confirmed each against the tool and fixed them all in one commit; round 1 approved. No finding was caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: A reference billed as complete was written from memory rather than read off the regex and key tables, which is where all five findings came from.
The lexical reply-hint said pushback on two threads whose replies plainly agreed.

evidence: CromGroup.invoke catches only CromError (agent verified cli.py:80-84), so an OSError from the new mkstemp escaped as a traceback. 2477865 guarded only the mkstemp call, leaving os.fdopen, the tail() open, and the finally unlink unguarded, which became F5, F7 and F8.
guidance_note: When adding a new filesystem boundary to a module that translates OSError at its other boundaries, list every OS call in the new code path (create, open, read, unlink) and decide each one's translation in the same change.

evidence: The cleanup leak is real and platform-independent: addCleanup was registered from launch's result, so any empty find_pids stranded the server. The Linux procps newline claim is not settled by the packet (the agent asserts it, the packet holds no Linux output). The fix writes stubs to a file and registers the kill before spawning.
guidance_note: Register cleanup for a spawned test process before spawning it, keyed on something the test owns, never on the return value under test.

evidence: The agent measured 5.3KB after 270s on default flags against 676KB in 90s under verbose logging, showing growth tracks activity rather than uptime. The truncate/rotate remedies need a live supervisor, and `crom up` exits after launch, so they were rejected. The docstring's "nothing anyone can see" overclaim was corrected and the residual deferred to a ticket.
guidance_note: When replacing DEVNULL with a real sink, state its unbounded-growth cost in the design comment instead of claiming it costs nothing.

evidence: Moving stderr from DEVNULL to a quoted error message newly let Chrome's (partly page-derived) bytes reach the terminal. 2477865 filters to `ch in "\n\t" or ch.isprintable()` inside tail(), the one boundary producing the string, with a mutation-checked escape test.
guidance_note: When routing bytes from an untrusted process into a user-facing message, sanitize control characters at the read boundary in the original change.

evidence: 2477865 wrapped only `tempfile.mkstemp` and left `os.fdopen(fd, "wb")` outside the guard, with a comment claiming a full temp dir was "the one way this fails". The agent also found the raw fd leaks if fdopen raises. 67d8358 replaced both calls with one NamedTemporaryFile inside one try.
guidance_note: When guarding a resource acquisition that spans two calls, guard both or collapse them into one call; check the second call's failure modes before writing "the one way this fails".

evidence: F1's fix added the OSError→CromError translation and the agent says it "verified that translation by hand last round and never committed the check". 67d8358 adds a ProcessBoundaryTest case asserting on launch(), mutation-checked.
guidance_note: When a fix adds an error translation at a boundary, commit the test that forces that boundary to fail in the same commit, next to the existing Popen/ps boundary tests.

evidence: The `finally: path.unlink()` predates the review, but it is another unguarded OS call in the same sink that F1's mkstemp-only fix did not sweep. An exception in finally does displace the in-flight CromError. The agent fixed the plausible case with `missing_ok=True` and kept read-only/NFS failures loud. Python chains the original as __context__, so nothing is silently lost.
guidance_note: When adding error translation to one call in a context manager, review its finally/teardown path for exceptions that could displace the one in flight.

evidence: tail()'s raw `open(self.path, "rb")` is another unguarded OS call in the sink F1's fix did not sweep. The agent noted tail() runs on the success path too, so a vanished file would crash a good launch. Instead of the reviewer's empty-transcript option, which would pass off a read failure as "Chrome printed nothing", the fix returns an explicit note.
guidance_note: When adding error translation to one call in a context manager, review its finally/teardown path for exceptions that could displace the one in flight.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the Popen stderr wiring is original-PR code, unchanged by 67d8358. Forked helpers inherit one open file description with one shared offset, so O_APPEND (which fixes separate descriptions racing) does not apply. The agent's six-process measurement showed 12,000/12,000 well-formed lines and no torn 64KB writes.

narrative: Adding stderr capture to Chrome launches created a new filesystem boundary. F1's fix guarded only the mkstemp call, without a test. Round 1 then found the unguarded fdopen (F5) and the missing test (F6), and round 2 found two more unguarded OS calls in the same sink (F7 teardown, F8 tail open). Round 2 also raised F9, an O_APPEND race the agent correctly refuted by measurement. A sweep of the sink's OS calls in the first fix would likely have converged at round 1, saving at least one round.
guidance_observations: The agent deliberately narrowed F1's guard to one call and did not enumerate the other OS calls in the same context manager, which produced four follow-on findings over two rounds.
The agent measured instead of arguing on F3 and F9, and both resolutions held.
